scalesUsed.notes: B - C# - D - E - F# - G - A - B
scalesUsed.application: Primary scale for melody and harmony throughout the song
Simplified scale for vocal melody contour and guitar embellishments

keyAndScale.relativeMinor: B minor is the relative minor of D major

mainProgression.description: Four-chord minor progression cycling through Bm-D-A-E, creating a cinematic, anthemic feel with the unexpected IV chord (E major) adding brightness

sectionProgressions.description: Subdued strumming over the same four-chord cycle, kept quiet to contrast with the explosive chorus
Same progression as verse but played with heavier attack, open strums, and more dynamic intensity
Shortened progression building tension and momentum into the chorus explosion

harmonicFunction: Bm (i) - Tonic minor, establishes the dark, brooding center of the song
D (III) - Relative major, brightens the harmony and provides lift
A (VII) - Subtonic major chord, creates openness and momentum
E (IV) - Subdominant, adds unexpected brightness borrowed from Dorian mode

techniques.name: Power Chord Strumming
techniques.description: Steady, rhythmic power chord strumming that forms the backbone of the song, alternating between muted ghost strums and open hits

notes: Bm: X-2-4-4-3-2 (barre chord) or simplified X-2-4-4-X-X (power chord)
D: X-X-0-2-3-2 (open D major)
A: X-0-2-2-2-0 (open A major)
E: 0-2-2-1-0-0 (open E major)
Use a steady eighth-note strumming pattern throughout
Verse strumming is lighter and more controlled
Chorus strumming opens up with full attack
sequence: Start with down-up eighth-note pattern on Bm
Transition smoothly to D on beat 3
Move to A for the next measure
Finish the cycle on E before returning to Bm
tips: Keep strumming hand moving in constant eighth-note motion even when muting
Use ghost strums (muted strings) to maintain rhythm during chord changes
Start with simplified chord shapes if barre chords are too difficult
Focus on the dynamic contrast between verse and chorus

techniques.name: Dynamic Contrast
techniques.description: The signature element of this song is the dramatic shift from quiet, restrained verses to explosive, powerful choruses

notes: Verse dynamics: play at around 30-40% volume with lighter touch
Pre-chorus: gradually increase strumming intensity
Chorus: full-volume strumming with open chords and strong attack
This quiet-loud dynamic is essential to the song's impact
sequence: Begin verse with soft, controlled strumming near the neck
Gradually move picking hand toward the bridge during pre-chorus
Hit the chorus with full downstrokes from the wrist
Pull back immediately for the next verse
tips: Practice the volume transition separately before combining with chord changes
Use picking hand position (neck vs bridge) to control tone and volume
The contrast is more important than the absolute volume level
Record yourself to check that the dynamic range is audible

techniques.name: Palm Muting
techniques.description: Light palm muting during verse sections creates a percussive, contained sound that contrasts with the open chorus

notes: Rest the edge of the picking hand lightly on the strings near the bridge
Apply just enough pressure to dampen sustain without fully muting
Used primarily during verse sections for rhythmic texture
Release palm mute for chorus sections to let chords ring out
sequence: Position palm edge on strings just in front of the bridge saddles
Strum with consistent eighth-note pattern while maintaining palm contact
Adjust pressure: lighter muting for a warmer sound, heavier for more percussive
Lift palm completely when transitioning to chorus
tips: The palm mute should soften the sound, not kill it completely
Practice finding the sweet spot where notes are dampened but still audible
Keep the wrist relaxed to avoid tension during extended palm-muted sections
Combine with lighter strumming for maximum verse-chorus contrast

sections.name: Intro
sections.description: Atmospheric opening with light percussive guitar and electronic elements establishing the Bm tonality before the vocals enter
notes: Guitar enters subtly beneath electronic percussion
Keep strumming very light and controlled
Establish the rhythmic pattern that continues into the verse
Listen for the drum pattern to lock in your timing

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: Quiet, restrained strumming over Bm-D-A-E with vocal melody carrying the section; guitar stays in the background
notes: Play softly to leave room for the vocal melody
Use light palm muting for a contained, percussive feel
Keep strumming pattern consistent but quiet
Two full cycles of the progression per verse

sections.name: Pre-Chorus
sections.description: Transitional section where dynamic intensity gradually increases, building anticipation for the powerful chorus
notes: Gradually increase strumming strength through this section
Release palm muting as you approach the chorus
Feel the energy building with each measure
The vocal builds here too - match its intensity

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: Explosive, full-volume strumming of the same Bm-D-A-E progression now played with maximum attack and open ringing chords
notes: This is where the song explodes - play with full conviction
Let all strings ring out without any palm muting
Use strong downstrokes mixed with up-strums for fullness
The contrast with the quiet verse is what makes this section powerful

sections.name: Bridge
sections.description: Brief bridge section with sustained chord hits and space, providing a moment of tension before the final chorus
notes: Sparser strumming with more space between chord hits
Let chords sustain and ring out
Creates tension through the reduced harmonic rhythm
Prepares for the final explosive chorus

sections.name: Outro
sections.description: Final repetition of the chorus progression that gradually fades with the chord cycle continuing to the end
notes: Maintain chorus energy initially
Gradually reduce intensity as the song fades
Final chord can be allowed to ring out and sustain
Match the recorded fade-out with a natural dynamic decrease

alternatives: Acoustic guitar (works well for stripped-down version)
guitar.pickup: Humbucker or single coil - clean to slight overdrive tone

amp.recommended: Fender Twin Reverb or similar clean amp
alternatives: Any clean-channel amp with slight breakup

effects.distortion: Light overdrive for chorus sections only
effects.other: Optional chorus or delay for atmospheric texture

beginner.focus: Learn the four basic chord shapes and establish a steady strumming pattern
steps: Learn open D, A, and E chord shapes - these are standard beginner chords
Practice the Bm barre chord or use a simplified two-finger power chord shape
Work on transitioning between all four chords smoothly at a slow tempo
Develop a consistent eighth-note down-up strumming pattern

intermediate.focus: Master the dynamic contrast between verse and chorus sections
steps: Practice playing the verse softly with palm muting technique
Work on the explosive transition from pre-chorus to chorus
Develop control over strumming dynamics from quiet to loud
Play along with the recording to match the feel and timing

advanced.focus: Refine tone, add embellishments, and perform the complete arrangement
steps: Dial in the amp and effects settings for authentic tone
Add subtle ghost strums and rhythmic variations to the strumming pattern
Practice seamless transitions between all song sections
Perform the complete song from memory with accurate dynamics

commonMistakes: Playing the verse too loud - the quiet-loud contrast is the heart of this song
Rushing chord changes and losing the steady 68 BPM tempo
Neglecting palm muting in the verse, making all sections sound the same
Struggling with the Bm barre chord and breaking rhythm during the change
practiceRoutine: Warm up with the four-chord cycle (Bm-D-A-E) at 50 BPM for 5 minutes
Practice palm muting on each chord individually for a clean dampened sound
Work on the dynamic shift: play 4 bars soft then 4 bars loud, alternating
Play through the full song structure with the recording at least twice
focusAreas: Clean chord transitions, especially to and from Bm barre chord
Steady eighth-note strumming rhythm without speeding up or slowing down
Dynamic control between whisper-quiet verses and powerful choruses
Palm muting technique for controlled, percussive verse tone
metronomeWork: Start at 50 BPM with quarter-note chord changes to build muscle memory
Increase to 68 BPM (song tempo) with full eighth-note strumming pattern
Practice the pre-chorus crescendo with metronome to keep tempo steady during buildup
Work on chord changes at 80 BPM to build comfort above song tempo
